punchline: Three years into running her own pie shop, the baker everyone praised said she couldn't stand the smell of pies.
thirty_sec: Sarah baked such good pies that her friends pushed her to open a shop. When Michael Gerber met her three years later, it was 7 a.m. She'd been up since two, she was crying, she kicked the oven and said she hated pies. Baking had become one small slice of a day of registers, bank runs and rent. Gerber's point: knowing the work isn't the same as knowing the business.
